newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Philips probes investor interest in Grundig.
newsitem.headline: Philips probes investor interest in Grundig.

text.p: Philips Electronics NV said on Thursday it was sounding out investors who might be interested in acquiring Grundig shares.
A spokesman said Philips was in talks with the Max Grundig Foundation about the Foundation's option to sell Philips its 52 percent stake in Grundig for 411 million marks in 2004.

"Anticipating the completion of the negotiations with the Grundig Foundation about their put option of 52 percent we are investigating possibilities to sell that 52 percent to interested third parties," said spokesman Ben Geerts.
"If the amount of interest is beyond 52 percent, Philips is prepared to reduce its 31.6 percent stake in Grundig as well," he added.

Geerts was responding to questions about a report in the Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung newspaper that Philips might sell its Grundig stake to small London merchant bank Botts & Co, which could lead to a private placement.

Philips is still in discussions with the Grundig family and the Max Grundig Foundation about disentangling links forged with Grundig in 1984, when the German business had a formidable brand presence in audio-visual products.
Last month the German firm, saddled for years with poor performances, reported a 631 million mark ($360 million) loss for 1996, compared to a 598 million mark loss the year before.
At the heart of the talks is the Max Grundig Foundation's put option and Philips' commitment to pay a 46 million mark a year dividend to the Grundig family heirs.
